column19: From every architect I have ever worked with in the last 6 years, there has been a clear precedent as to the importance of your work in the discipline of architecture. Architecture is designs made by humans, for humans. A generative Artificial Intelligence will NEVER and can NEVER replace the characteristics of a human, as it will never truly envision or live within a building that it "designs". The decision to incorporate generative AI implicates that the department does not believe in its students, and while it attempts to raise the floor for minimum quality work, does not at all attempt to raise the ceiling as far as the detail for architectural creation. A student, at this rate, is fully expected to work completely proactively, or in my experience, work directly at the whim of the professor, lest receive a lower grade for not producing deliverables that meet the expectation of the project's rubric or design standard. For as long as I remain here at Texas A&M I will fully fight the incorporation of generative AI software. A tool is not a solution.
